description:
Front
T1	False Acacia x 1 (Robinia pseudoacacia) This 12m mature Robinia has severe die back in the crown. The top 3m are stone dead with large cracks in the bark exposing decaying heartwood. There are fungal fruiting bodies around the base, indicating 
root decay. There tree leans towards the house but is alongside the public footpath. Any failure would cause significant damage. Suggested work:
- fell to ground level using advanced rigging techniques
- poison stump to prevent the root system sending up suckers
Client happy to replant significant tree (5m with 12-14cm girth).

Justification : Tree is in severe decline, it is half dead, it has a lean, mushrooms at the base, and all of that is a large risk to the public.
Front
T2	Mulberry x 1	This 8m mature mulberry tree has grown too large for the client to be able to pick the fruit. It is also encroaching upon the 
property. 
Suggested work:-AMENDMENT AS AGREED VIA EMAIL 18/08/26. Re-reduce to previous points. 

Recommend mulberry pruned January - March 2027

The justification is the tree is too big, it has been pruned previously and now needs pruning again. Its close to the house and encroaches on the footpath, a reduction will make the tree smaller.
application_type_full: Tree works: Trees in conservation areas/subject to TPOs
decision_conditions:
TREE WORKS (COMPLIANCE):  All tree work shall be carried out in accordance with British Standard BS3998 - Recommendations for Tree Work.  In addition: 
a)   No fires shall be lit within [10] metres of the nearest point of the canopy of any retained tree.  No equipment, machinery or structure shall be attached to or supported by a retained tree.
b)   No mixing of cement or use of other contaminating materials or substances shall take place within, or close enough to, a root protection area that seepage or displacement could cause them to enter a root protection area. 
c)   No alterations or variations to the approved works or tree protection schemes shall be made without prior written consent of the local planning authority.

REASON:  In the interest of the protection of trees and to safeguard visual amenities.
